resources.string: Setup
Prepare device
For RedMonitor to run reliably on your %1$s device, you need to relax a few limits depending on the manufacturer. We\'ll walk through them step by step here.
Device
Android %1$s (SDK %2$d)
Xiaomi devices restrict apps the most - every step below matters here.
Xiaomi-specific: lock in Recents
In the Recents screen (overview of all open apps) long-press the RedMonitor card and tap \'Lock\' / the padlock. This lets the app survive the \'Close all\' swipe and the MIUI Memory Cleaner.
Samsung-specific: Sleeping apps
Settings -> Battery -> Background usage limits -> Sleeping apps. RedMonitor must NOT be in this list. If it is: remove it.
Shizuku (for Logcat, Tasks, Doze, ...)
Shizuku gives this app shell-user rights without root. Needed for: reading Logcat, finding the top-CPU app, managing the Doze whitelist, force-stopping apps.
Shizuku status
Status & setup steps if not ready yet.

Remind me later (don\'t show at startup again)
Aggressive background limits - allow autostart explicitly.
\'MIUI optimization\' in developer options can interfere with Shizuku/ADB - turn it off if there are problems.
\'Show pop-ups while running in background\' required for live updates.
Memory cleanup can kill the app in the background - \'Lock\' it in the Recents screen.
Battery optimization & \'Sleeping apps\' otherwise block updates.
Game Booster / Edge panel can block the overlay.
Enable ColorOS autostart + \'Allow running in background\'.
Raise background power usage + allow \'background calls\'.
Manage app launch manually - turn all three toggles ON.
Restricted app standby bucket can slow the app down.
